paper_title: Knowledge Crosswords Geometric Knowledge Reasoning with Large Language   Models
caption: Problem distribution based on the correctness under the w/ knowledge and w/o knowledge settings using Zero-Shot.
model_annotation: The figure displays three pie charts illustrating the distribution of problem correctness across three difficulty levels—easy, medium, and hard—under the Zero-Shot setting, comparing outcomes with and without knowledge. Each chart is segmented by four categories represented by distinct colors: N+K+ (teal), N−K+ (light yellow), N−K− (orange), and N+K− (red), with a legend provided on the right. In the "easy" category, N+K+ accounts for 55.4%, N−K+ for 38.3%, and N+K− for 4.6%, with N−K− at 1.7%. For "medium" problems, N+K+ makes up 58.8%, N−K+ 35.4%, N+K− 4.0%, and N−K− 1.8%. In the "hard" category, N−K+ is the largest segment at 37.9%, followed by N+K+ at 37.3%, N−K− at 18.1%, and N+K− at 6.7%. All percentages are labeled within the respective slices of the pie charts, and the slices are arranged in descending order of size within each chart.
